title: WPMS/2825/2021 of SEKHAR SINGH PAPOLA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2825 of 2021
Sekhar Singh Papola ... Petitioner
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others ... Respondents
Advocates : Mr. D.K. Joshi, Advocate, for the petitioner
 Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, Standing Counsel, for the State of Uttarakhand
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
On 9th June 2016, the petitioner as plaintiff No. 1, had
instituted a suit, being Suit No. 33 of 2016, Sekhar Singh
Papola and Another Vs. Thakur Singh and others, for the
grant of decree of a permanent injunction, in relation to the
properties, which were described in the relief clause, which is
extracted hereunder :-

उिचत समझेवह िड्ቅी भी वादीगण को िदलायी जाय।"
2. The said Suit proceeded on its merits, and it was
decided by the learned Court of Civil Judge (Senior
Division), Bageshwar, by way of Original Suit No. 13 of
2019, Shekhar Singh Papola Vs. Thakur Singh and others,
vide its judgement and decree dated 29th February 2020,
which had been later on affirmed in a Civil Appeal, being
Civil Appeal No. 2 of 2020, by the judgement and decree,

2
which had been rendered by the Court of Additional District
Judge, on 15th February 2021.
In the Suit thus instituted by the petitioner, State and
Executive Engineer of the Public Works Department, were
impleaded as defendant Nos. 2 and 3 respectively. Meaning
thereby, the suit thus concurrently decided in favour of
defendants therein, will have an equal binding effect on the
parties to the Suit itself, however, the concurrent judgements
which were rendered by the learned Civil Court, in relation to
the same set of property; was now the subject matter of
consideration in a Second Appeal, being Second Appeal
No. 70 of 2021, Shekhar Singh Papola and others Vs.
Thakur Singh and others, which had been instituted by the
appellant-petitioner herein, through the same counsel on 27th
July 2021.
3. There had been yet another Second Appeal, being
Second Appeal No. 71 of 2021, Shekhar Singh Papola and
others Vs. Thakur Singh and others, which had been
preferred by the appellant-petitioner herein, challenging the
judgement, which had been passed by the Courts below, as
deciding the issue No. 3, in Suit No. 13 of 2019, Shekhar
Singh Papola Vs. Thakur Singh and others. The decision
which was taken on issue No. 3, pertained to, as to whether
the suit would be barred by the principle of res judicata? The
same had been decided in the light of the provisions
contained under Section 11 of the C.P.C., which later on
stood affirmed in Civil Appeal, being Civil Appeal No. 2 of

3
2020, Shekhar Singh Papola Vs. Thakur Singh and others,
and in these proceedings thus decided by the competent civil
Court, a concurrent finding has been recorded against the
appellant/petitioner. Against this judgement too, another
Second Appeal, being Second Appeal No. 71 of 2021,
Shekhar Singh Papola and others Vs. Thakur Singh and
others, is pending consideration, which had been preferred
by the same counsel by filing the same before the Registry of
this Court on 27th July 2021.
4. Its not only that, rather the petitioner had approached
this Court, by filing earlier writ petition being Writ Petition
(M/S) No. 214 of 2013, Shekhar Singh Papola Vs. State of
Uttarakhand and others as aggrieved against the order
which was passed by the respondents, which was disposed of
by the coordinate Bench of this Court with the direction to
the District Magistrate, to decide the representation of the
petitioner.
5. In the earlier writ petition, the cause, which was
agitated by the petitioner was with regards to the alleged act
of encroachment by respondent number 8, herein, who was
the defendant No. 1, in the Suit against category 5 land, lying
in khata No. 23, as described in para 27 of the present writ
petition.
6. Through the same counsel, the petitioner had preferred
this writ petition on 5th December 2021, after admittedly
knowing the fact of filing of the Second Appeal and during

4
its pendency, modulating the relief in the writ petition in the
following manner:-
"PRAYER
It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may
graciously be pleased to:
i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing
the respondents to restrain the private respondents no. 7 & 8 from
carrying out the transportation of miner minerals over illegally
constructed road in the area of Village Gulam Pargarh and Nargara,
Tehsil Kapkot, District Bageshwar.
ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondents to take strict legal action against the
private respondents no. 7 & 8 for the damage caused to the public
land by committing illegal activities over the said land as mentioned
above.
iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondents to review/recall Government Order dated
16.08.2017 issued in favour of private addressees and Government
Order dated 19.08.2000 issued in favour of private addresses
whereby the lease has been granted for excavation and quarrying of
mines and minerals.
iv) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
directing the respondents to set up a high level committee to enquire
into the matter and further to take legal action against the erring
persons including the responsible authorities.
v) Issue a writ, order or direction, which this Hon'ble Court may
think fit and proper in the circumstances of the case. Award the
cost."
7. In fact, the modulation of the relief itself, if it is taken
into consideration in the light of pleadings of the writ
petition, it was qua the property, which was the subject
matter, for which the relief was sought for, has been
described by the petitioner himself in the writ petition, which
happens to be the same property, which was the subject
matter of the Suit, against which the Second Appeal is
pending consideration. In fact, resorting to institution of the

5
subsequent writ petition on 5th December 2021, was nothing,
but an intelligible device which had been adopted by the
petitioner to override the effect of the judgement and decree,
which had been concurrently decided by the competent
regular Civil Courts, with regard to the same set of land,
which was described in the plaint and which has been
described in the present writ petition in para 27. Not even
that, this writ petition would be barred by the provisions
contained under Section 11, to be read with Order 2 Rule 2 of
the CPC, when his earlier Writ Petition No. 214 of 2013,
was already decided on 8th March 2013, and it was thereafter
only that the suit was instituted by the petitioner, before the
Civil Court on 9th June 2016, that means much after the
earlier judgement of Writ Petition No. 214 of 2013, which
had been decided by a coordinate Bench of this Court on 8th
March 2013.
8. In fact, this is a fit case where the record itself reveals
that it is an apparent abuse of process of law Court, which
has been deliberately and concurrently adopted by the
petitioner to override the effect of the judgement and decree,
which has been concurrently rendered by the competent Civil
Court, which is still the subject matter of Second Appeal,
which was instituted the appellant-petitioner herein on 27th
July 2021 through the same counsel, who is the counsel in
the present writ petition.
9. The distinction, which has been attempted to be carved
out by the learned counsel for the petitioner, is that in fact,

6
the writ petition would not be barred, because of the fact that
the Second Appeal is pending consideration, because here, in
the present writ petition, it is an inaction on part of the State
agencies, which has been impleaded therein as respondent
Nos. 1 to 6, to the writ petition, who had been attributed with
the responsibility to curb the activity, for which the relief has
been sought for in the writ petition pertaining to same piece
of land, the fact which is not disputed by the counsel.
10. In fact, this plea of the petitioner that the writ petition
would not be barred, because it is rather the inaction of the
State, which is the subject matter of challenge in the present
writ petition, is not acceptable by this Court, for the reason
being that in the Suit, which was preferred by the petitioner,
in fact, the State agency were impleaded as one of the
contesting defendant, to the Suit and in that eventuality, the
inter se rights between the defendants therein and the State,
qua the petitioner, in relation to the same set of property
stood decided by the competent civil Court at the behest of
the proceedings, which had been instituted by the petitioner
himself who had opted for State to be defendant in the Suit,
and once he has submitted to the judgement of earlier writ
petition, which was rendered in 2013, and had admittedly
later preferred a Suit subsequently in 2016, and having lost
concurrently from both the Courts and thereafter preferred
the Second Appeals before this Court on 27th July 2021,
which are still pending consideration it goes without saying
that the petitioner was conscious of the fact that he has
already agitated a cause in relation to the same set of

7
properties in the Second Appeal, as well as, in the earlier writ
petition, and a clever distinction which has been sought to be
carved out, that in the writ petition, it entails the act of the
State agencies, which has been a subject matter, in fact, is
nothing but the misnomer on part of the petitioner to distract
and deviate the Court from the affect and the consequences
of the Civil Decree, concurrently rendered against him and as
already observed above, this delicacy of argument of the
learned counsel for the petitioner of drawing a distinction
from the prospective, that writ petition engages consideration
of an inaction on part of the State agency, is the concept
which is not acceptable by this Court, while the petitioner
himself, as a plaintiff in the suit has chosen the State and the
Executive Engineer, Public Works Department, as to be one
of the defendant and therein also, it was the same property
subject matter, hence, this Court is of a considered view that
the present writ petition is a clever and intentional device
adopted by the petitioner to overcome the effect of the
embargoes being faced by him by the respective rights
decided by the Civil Court, which is the subject matter of
Second Appeal, since the writ petition itself had been
preferred on 5th December 2021 i.e. much after filing of the
Second Appeal.
11. What is more important to be observed is that the
Second Appeal, being Second Appeal Nos. 70 of 2021 and
71 of 2021, which had been preferred by the petitioner as
against the regular concurrent decree of competent Civil
Court, when it was instituted before this Court on 27th July

8
2021, it was marked as defective, and the appellant therein
was granted time by the coordinate Bench to remove the
defect, which was not done till 23rd August 2021. Hence, in
fact, there operates no interim protection in the Second
Appeal, which had been preferred by the petitioner, hence,
preferring the writ petition on 5th December 2021, this Court
is of the view, that it is a conscious and a deliberate act, on
part of the petitioner and its counsel too (common in all cases
before this Court), for resorting to a concurrent proceedings
in relation to the same set of land, which constitutes to be the
part of a decree of the Civil Court, hence the present writ
petition happens to be the best example of an apparent abuse
of process of law Court.
12. The concept of abuse of process of Court of law is one
of the core issues, which has to be taken care of in the present
judicial scenario, where a deliberate and intentional efforts
are being made by the litigant on his failure to procure a
favourable order in a pre-instituted proceedings to institute a
fresh case under other provisions of law in relation to the
same subject matter, or a same subject and if resort to the
aforesaid process is with a clever intent, which is reflected in
the present case where in almost all the cases it is the same
counsel, who has filed the proceedings before this Court in
relation to the same set of property and almost for a similar
relief it is he who is to be blamed with, that he has not
approached the Court with clean hands and it deliberately
abuses the process of law Court. This is what has been held
by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment reported in 2008

9
(1) SCC 560, Udyami Evam Khadi Gramodyog Welfare
Sanstha and Another Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and others,
where, in para 10 and 16, which are extracted hereunder:-
"10. Although the prayers made in the four writ applications
are apparently different, having gone through the writ
applications, it became evident that the core issue in each of
the matter centers round recovery of the amount advanced to
the appellants by the bank. Evidently, orders passed in
different stages of the proceedings as also new proceedings
based upon fresh calculation on interest on the principal sum
had been in question from time to time. As indicated
hereinbefore, even a public interest litigation was filed
wherein also Appellant No. 2 was a party. Maybe that validity
of Section 35A of the U.P. Khadi and Village Industries
Board Act, 1960 was one of the issues raised therein but even
the recovery proceeding was the subject matter thereof.
16. A writ remedy is an equitable one. A person approaching
a superior court must come with a pair of clean hands. It not
only should not suppress any material fact, but also should
not take recourse to the legal proceedings over and over again
which amounts to abuse of the process of law. In Advocate
General, State of Bihar v. M/s. Madhya Pradesh Khair
Industries and Another [(1980) 3 SCC 311], this Court was of
the opinion that such a repeated filing of writ petitions
amounts to criminal contempt."
13. The said principles has been laid down, based upon the
earlier ratio of the Hon'ble Apex Court, particularly, that as
considered therein in the matter of Advocate General, State
of Bihar Vs. M.P. Khair Industries that equitable remedy if it
is approached by a person it has to be approached with clean
hands. Concealment of fact or distortion of fact with an
intention to procure an order in his favour cannot be
permitted to be perpetuated in the judicial system of this
country.
14. The learned counsel for the petitioner, faced with the
aforesaid observations, which were carried during the course
of the argument of the present writ petition, prayed for that

10
he may be permitted to file a rejoinder affidavit, in
compliance of the earlier order dated 6th May 2022, in the
given set of circumstances, and for the reasons which have
already been discussed above.
15. First of all, under the High Court's Rules, filing of a
rejoinder is not as a matter of right and hence, the request for
filing of the rejoinder affidavit, to the counter affidavit in the
present writ petition is denied. Secondly, after being faced
with the situation, emerging during the arguments as
extended by learned counsel for the petitioner in the present
writ petition at length, and faced with the peculiar
circumstances, where the petitioner is already pursuing his
remedy in the Second Appeal, in relation to the same set of
properties, he made a prayer that the writ petition may be
permitted to be dismissed as withdrawn. This Court declines
the said prayer, because this Court cannot be permitted to be
put to test by litigants, that as soon as the writ petition is
preferred by the petitioner and has filed the same before the
Registry of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution
of India, for enforcement of a civil right or constitutional or
legal statutory right, protected under law, after its institution,
it is no more a choice, which is left open to the wisdom of the
petitioner to get it withdrawn and that too, in the
circumstances of the present case, when the petitioner has
faced with the situation already discussed above.
16. Hence, the request for dismissing the writ petition as
withdrawn is declined, considering the fact:

11
One, the property as described in the writ petition and in the
Civil Suit remains the same;
Second, in the Civil Suit, the State agency was already party;
Third, the petitioner has already been adjudicated as a
judgement-debtor by the regular Civil Court;
Fourth, the petitioner has earlier filed a writ petition even
prior to filing of the Suit, which was disposed of in 2013;
Fifth, the petitioner admittedly had preferred a Second
Appeal, which was defective and the defect was not cured by
the petitioner till August 2021;
Sixth, when he filed this writ petition on 5th December 2021,
if all these facts were consciously known to the petitioner, as
well as his counsel, who happens to be same in all the cases,
because he happens to be the common in all the proceedings,
a professional fairness was expected from him, who is
engaged in this noble profession.
17. Hence, this writ petition is dismissed with a cost of Rs.
1.00 lakh, to be deposited by the petitioner in the High Court
Bar Association Advocates' Welfare Fund. If the amount of
cost is not deposited in one month, the Collector of District
Bageshwar, would ensure its recovery.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
18.05.2022
Mahinder/
